responseContracts.v1Choose: Suffix selection. Accepted alternate counters must not be wrong distractors.
responseContracts.v1Type: Authored suffix and complete counting-phrase forms under legacy rules; no claim that only complete phrases are accepted. Kana alternatives belong to this answer set, not automatically to Read.
responseContracts.v1Read: Only the displayed canonical phrase through readingAnswers. Thus 一部 remains いちぶ even when 組/セット are accepted for Type.
responseContracts.v1Reverse: 頭 versus the actual displayed nouns 牛, ノート, ペン, 車. No hidden forward sentence supplies context.
responseContracts.v1EnglishContextCaveat: The published content contract at docs\counter-n5.md:79-80 puts full English translations after checking. F1 therefore does not count the en field as a pre-answer restriction. No app implementation was inspected.
responseContracts.v2: Write/Read only. Explicit authored written forms; NFKC/whitespace handling is not arithmetic or numeral normalization. Read pronounces the canonical written field, not every allowed writing.
responseContracts.grammar: External answer slot. Arabic digits only, no unit/comma, explicitly requested. Do not supply a missing Japanese fragment or silently accept additional numeral representations.

decision.2: contrast or interpretation of the requested entity/quantity

ambiguity.0: one fair answer or visible convention
ambiguity.2: hidden guessing or unaccepted ordinary alternative

feedback.2: compares a nearby wrong answer or mistaken interpretation

scoringNotes: Higher feedback is good; these dimensions are not summed into a difficulty score.
Ordinary orthographic alternatives can earn ambiguity 1 without indicating a defect.
Number-to-language/notation transcoding is calculation 0. Computing an amount removed/remaining is calculation 1, including a transparent complement.
Decision scores describe the actual prompted operation, not the most advanced distinction mentioned only in feedback.

The reverse record has no own explanation field, so its feedback score is 0. If a presentation reuses the linked cow note, that presentation would offer more feedback; this review does not assert that the UI shows none.

initialFindings.claim: The exclusion of a bound booklet is stated only in en and note, although 冊 is a wrong choice. The Japanese 三枚で一組の資料 establishes a three-sheet set, not that it is unbound. Under the documented answer-side English contract, the learner does not receive the physical-state restriction used to justify rejecting 冊.
initialFindings.impact: A learner can reasonably picture a short bound/stapled handout and select 冊; the explanation then reveals an unstated fact. This is a question-context defect, not a claim that 冊 counts genuinely loose sheets.
initialFindings.minimalCorrection: Put the restriction in the question-side Japanese, for example 三枚一組の、とじていない資料を、一{}コピーしてください。, and gloss とじていない as not bound/stapled. Keep complete-copy versus individual-sheet wording. Alternatively provide an actually visible context field; do not rely on en or feedback.
initialFindings.confidence: high that the restriction is absent from Japanese; medium-high for the resulting ordinary booklet interpretation
initialFindings.qualification: If a separately demonstrated current presentation shows en before answering, the visibility portion must be reassessed. This report follows the documented contract, without a device or implementation check.

initialFindings.claim: The intended loose complete-set context licenses ordinary Type alternatives beyond the stored list: ワンセット/わんせっと, the spelling 一組み, and 一式/いっしき. None is authored. The task does not visibly restrict the answer to 部 or to the exact spelling 組.
initialFindings.impact: Correct complete-set responses can be rejected despite 組 and セット already being accepted. This remains after making the loose-paper context visible.
initialFindings.minimalCorrection: Add 組み/一組み and 一式 (plus 式 if following this family's suffix/full-phrase convention) to fitting written forms, ワンセット to fitting written forms, and わんせっと/いっしき to kana or an explicitly explained accepted tier. Preserve canonical phrase 一部 and readingAnswers=[いちぶ]. Do not put an entire ワンセット into an unchanged 一{} display; use the established complete-phrase replacement contract.
initialFindings.confidence: high for ワンセット and 組み; medium-high for contextual 一式
initialFindings.qualification: Sources establish set senses, spelling and readings; the applicability to this specifically one-set copying request is the reviewer's contextual judgment. This does not authorize every dictionary synonym or every loan-number reading for every counter.

initialRecordAssessments.judgment: Natural 牧場で牛を一頭見ました. 頭 is the model, 匹 is a permissible broader animal count in this ordinary observation. 一頭=いっとう; Type's いっぴき is not a reading of 一頭. 冊/台/杯 are wrong here. 牧場 is supported without leaking the counter.

Natural zoo sentence and clear English. 六頭=ろくとう; 六匹=ろっぴき fits the accepted animal-count alternative, without migrating into canonical Read. No selected distractor is a normal counter for these elephants. This is principally the same animal-class operation as the cow, not independently demonstrated transfer.

施設では and 訓練を受けています are natural. 施設/盲導犬/訓練/受けています have appropriate readings and glosses. 頭 for working dogs is supported; 匹 is not categorically wrong. Both はっとう/はちとう and Type-only はっぴき/はちひき are documented. Feedback explains the preference but does not directly diagnose a particular wrong option.

Reviewed actual noun choices from the frozen addendum: 牛, ノート, ペン, 車. Only 牛 normally takes 頭. No farm sentence, notebook purchase, pen location or car-parking context is needed or assumed. The alternate counters on the pen dependency do not make 頭 valid for ペン. No reverse-specific rationale is authored.

一部/いちぶ is correct; 部/組/セット preserve the intended complete three-sheet unit, while one 枚 does not. ひとくみ is appropriate for a set, not the class-label reading いちくみ. The stored いっせっと/いちせっと/ひとせっと are supported rather than erroneous. Read must remain いちぶ. Loose status is not in the Japanese question, and ordinary set alternatives remain unlisted.

The Japanese itself states one sheet. Eight complete copies and eight sheets therefore coincide: 部/枚 are both accepted, with はちぶ/はちまい correctly separated from canonical Read. 頭/台/杯 are fair wrong suffixes. 申込書 is glossed accurately. Unlike the loose-handout exclusion, the decisive context is question-side.

同じ本 supplies the same-publication condition required for 部; 冊 counts the bound physical books and is correctly accepted. 六部=ろくぶ, 六冊=ろくさつ. 枚/頭/杯 do not preserve this ordinary request. 注文しました is supported. Feedback explains the overlap, rather than directly comparing one selected wrong answer.

123,000,000=1億2300万; いちおくにせんさんびゃくまん is correct. The explicitly required digits before both units and prohibition of commas/千/百/人 make the one written answer fair. Not a population inference or arithmetic story; numerical regrouping is the language skill.

100,030,000 yen=一億三万円, not 130,000,000. All four ordinary kanji/Arabic choices for the two numeral positions are authored. Zero groups are not pronounced. The plain-digit prohibition is visible. This extends the control's zero-gap grouping, rather than proving a harder semantic decision.

Two thirds is 三分の二/さんぶんのに; the four ordinary numeral combinations are accepted. Required 分の excludes a percentage/decimal without hidden normalization. Feedback directly corrects the reversed fraction. Source label 分数/ぶんすう avoids a metadata collision with minute 分/ふん.

数十人/すうじゅうにん is correct. The required initial 数, kanji 十 and 人 make the written convention explicit. 十数人 is contrasted without falsely assigning an exact headcount or an exclusive 11-19 boundary. This highly scaffolded form task is not an independent open interpretation test.

20% off is 二割引/にわりびき, with optional written き and both numeral spellings. The requested reduction rate is not the final price or 80% payable. No charge assumptions are imported. This expresses a form; it does not substitute for the Grammar quantity decision.

The counted entity is one packed box, not six cookies. 一箱/1箱/ひと箱 and canonical ひとはこ are fitting. IMABI's actual 箱 table explicitly lists イッぱこ alongside ひとはこ, so accepting いっぱこ is evidence-based. Sanabo confirms ひとはこ only; that omission does not refute the alternate. No equal-frequency or aural-acceptance claim is made.

第三課/第3課 and だいさんか correctly identify lesson 3. 第 is expressly requested; not accepting bare 三課 is a visible notation convention, not a universal ban. The answer does not imply three lessons completed.

Three different lessons completed is a quantity: 三課/3課, さんか. Explicitly excluding 第/目 distinguishes count from label. It does not disclose the final lesson's identifier. The pair contrasts semantic operations, not merely two numbers.

一秒=いちびょう without a false contraction. Optional written 間 is explicit and all four numeral/unit forms are listed. Canonical Read must not add かん. A useful easy unit item, not evidence that every new level-3 item is harder than the duration control.

一分三十秒=いっぷんさんじゅうびょう. All 16 combinations of kanji/Arabic components, optional と, and optional final 間 are authored. The visible convention excludes 90秒 and intermediate 間; those are not silently normalized. Accepted writing variants do not add と/かん to canonical Read.

Natural notice, explicitly no other charges. The question asks the reduction: 1000×2/10=200. 800 is the payable amount and has a useful wrong-option explanation. Digits-only response convention is explicit; 千円/二割引 are protected from vocabulary help, while 定価/料金 and other supporting words are correctly glossed.

The same notice asks a different quantity: the complementary 80%, 800 yen. 200 is a fair nearest wrong answer, not an accepted alternate. No hidden tax/fee ambiguity remains. One transparent complement, not a multi-step story. Same shop-discount context as its pair.

Natural report; その refers to the original 300 mL. One third used means 100; 200 instead remains. Supporting ボトル/水/ありました/使いました readings and senses are accurate. 三百ミリリットル and 三分の一 are unglossed target quantities, not accidentally omitted supporting vocabulary.

The explicit immediately-after/no-other-changes condition makes 200 mL remaining determinate. 100 is the part used, not another valid answer. Digits-only external answer slot and protected numerical vocabulary are correct. Shares water-fraction with the used-amount item, not a third/fourth independent context.

Verified identical to HEAD. 10,100円=一万百円/いちまんひゃくえん; all six written answers preserve it. 円 rather than a currency symbol is explicit. Feedback explains grouping but its generic sound-change list does not diagnose the particularly relevant zero-gap error. This already tests skipped positions below 万.

Verified identical to HEAD. 二時間半/にじかんはん is correct. Authored half-hour, minute and decimal representations are equivalent writing choices under the hours-required cue. The explicit no-と convention is fair. None authorizes reading 三十分 in place of displayed 半. At least as composed as the new minute-second item; no difficulty increase is inferred.

Verified identical to HEAD. Three children get two stickers each: total 6, not per-child 2. The external digits-only response and all rationale branches agree. 三人/二枚 vocabulary supports quantities without giving the total or glossing away the target ずつ relation. Its established jlpt=3 is not transferable evidence for the new fraction/discount construction.

limits: Public search tool failed; some simplified dictionary pages returned only chrome or irrelevant entries. Claims above rely on the actual named sections subsequently inspected, not on search hits.
The attempted Sanabo elephant URL redirected to 造花 and was excluded as evidence. A guessed set entry was 404 and excluded.
The supplied source catalog was not treated as verification. Sources were fetched independently.
No exhaustive pronunciation dictionary or corpus was downloaded. No regional/archaic reading completeness claim is made.
Exact native frequency of いっぱこ is not established by this bounded check, but its recognition is explicitly supported. Canonical ひとはこ remains the teaching model.

No independent exhaustive negative search of Bunpro was made. Omission of jlpt is justified by lack of a positive exact construction anchor in this reviewed evidence, not proof that no conceivable index entry exists.

authorComparison.policy: Preserve the independent initial scores for this review, with the qualifications below. Calibration differences alone are not new linguistic findings or empirically measured difficulty.

adjudications.judgment: The author assigns 1 to all 24 records. Under the requested definition, 20 complete records compare a nearby wrong answer/reading/interpretation and merit 2. Important evidence includes the Grammar wrong-option rationales, not only the top-level explanation. Three records remain 1. The reverse record has no own explanation field and is 0, with the already recorded caveat that a renderer might reuse the linked cow note; no UI absence claim is made.
adjudications.impact: Calibration correction, mostly favorable to the content; not 21 defects.

adjudications.judgment: Handout 2 versus author 1 is consequential and tied to F1/F2. The other ten differences are a declared scale choice: the independent review uses 1 for explicit ordinary written/read variants, while the author often uses 0 because the intended meaning is determinate. Both can describe fair tasks; use one convention consistently for old and new records. Neither ten spelling differences nor the higher score implies ten flawed tasks.
adjudications.impact: One actual problematic record; otherwise calibration only.

adjudications.judgment: The independent review treats writing 123,000,000 in 億/万, retaining zero groups, and expressing 20% using 割 as language/notation transcoding (0), not story calculation. This is consistent with the unchanged price control's grouping score. Actual reduction, complement and ずつ-total computations stay 1. The author's 1 for the two magnitude forms and discount-rate form is a different definition, not evidence that they are empirically harder.
adjudications.impact: Keep transparent calculation separate from lexical/notation conversion.

adjudications.judgment: The independent review uses 0 for isolated reverse noun association, versus author 1. It uses 2 for the one-sheet/complete-copy overlap, boxes versus contents, and the two lesson label/count contrasts, versus author 1. These count explicit contrast in the requested entity/meaning even when heavily scaffolded; they are not claims of open inference, harder Japanese or independent mastery. The four Grammar interpretations and ずつ control agree at 2.
adjudications.impact: A granularity difference; retain both vectors in the record rather than claiming experimental disagreement.

adjudications.judgment: The independent review counts a few glossed supporting words in the cow, publication and sticker-control records as 1, versus author 0 for familiar/supported words. The rubric's 0/1 descriptions overlap at this boundary. Neither review finds specialized unexplained load 2; no content change is required merely to align these scores.

Added 組み/一組み, 式/一式, ワンセット and fitting kana forms. Canonical 一部/いちぶ and readingAnswers remain unchanged.

Production CounterGrader accepts only authored kana plus the canonical counterReading. Added kana stems for already-accepted alternate written counters: くみ/しき, まい, さつ and ひき on the six new forward cards. Read metadata is untouched; ordinary kana Type alternatives remain the existing Yellow tier.

findingReconciliation.observedCorrection: とじていない三枚一組の資料を、一{}コピーしてください。
findingReconciliation.judgment: Natural Japanese makes the relevant unbound condition question-side. Three sheets form one set, and とじていない rules out the bound-booklet interpretation previously left open. The matching glossary reading とじていない and gloss not bound or stapled together are accurate, context-appropriate support and do not supply the target counter. The revised note explains the same fact already available to the learner.
findingReconciliation.distractorAssessment: 一枚 counts one sheet rather than the requested three-sheet copy; 冊 is not the unit for the explicitly unbound set; 台 is wrong here. No answer-side English is now needed to establish the physical-state restriction.

findingReconciliation.judgment: The specific ordinary complete-set forms identified by F2 are now authored and fit the tightened one-complete-copy scenario. Their inclusion does not require accepting every dictionary synonym. The canonical phrase and canonical-only Read set are correctly unchanged.
findingReconciliation.qualification: The original enumerated F2 omissions are closed. The separate remaining bare セット/せっと alias issue is F3 below, arising in the expressly disclosed stem-alias follow-up.

findingReconciliation.judgment: Every added stem is a valid bare kana name/form of a written counter already accepted in that same task. Existing Yellow treatment is appropriate under the supplied v1 Type policy; it must not imply that the Japanese is incorrect. These are suffix-mode aliases, not new readings of the displayed canonical counting phrase.

findingReconciliation.canonicalReadingBoundary: Bare ひき does not make いちひき a reading of 一匹, and none of these stems is a reading of the displayed 一頭/六頭/八頭 or 一部/八部/六部. No such incorrect full readings were added.

remainingFindingAtThatSnapshot.minimalCorrection: Add the single string せっと to bu-handout-1.kana. Leave good, phrase=一部, reading=いちぶ and readingAnswers=[いちぶ] unchanged.
remainingFindingAtThatSnapshot.scopeQualification: This is not a request for another synonym, a new counter, numeral normalization or app implementation work. It completes the same disclosed bare-stem alias policy already applied to 組/式/枚/冊/匹.
